gloss: stage fright; nervousness in front of others

definitions.gloss: stage fright; performance anxiety; tendency to get nervous in front of others
definitions.explanation: A personality trait or tendency to become extremely nervous when speaking in public, performing, or being the center of attention. Can refer to both the condition and the person who has it.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}はあがり{症|しょう}だ。
あがり{症|しょう}を{克服|こくふく}したい。
examples.english: I want to overcome my stage fright.

examples.japanese: あがり{症|しょう}なので、{大勢|おおぜい}の{前|まえ}でスピーチするのがとても{苦手|にがて}だ。
examples.english: Since I have stage fright, I'm very bad at giving speeches in front of a large audience.

notes:
Composed of あがる (to get nervous, to freeze up) and {症|しょう} (condition, tendency). Describes a habitual tendency to become nervous in social performance situations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- あがり{症|しょう}を{克服|こくふく}する: to overcome stage fright
- あがり{症|しょう}を{治|なお}す: to cure one's stage fright
- ひどいあがり{症|しょう}: severe stage fright
- あがり{症|しょう}の{人|ひと}: a person with stage fright

USAGE:
Can be used both as a noun describing the condition (あがり{症|しょう}を{克服|こくふく}する) and as a predicate describing a person ({私|わたし}はあがり{症|しょう}だ). As a na-adjective modifier: あがり{症|しょう}な{人|ひと}.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {緊張|きんちょう}: nervousness, tension — a temporary state, not a habitual trait
- あがり{症|しょう}: stage fright — a personality trait or habitual tendency
- {人見知|ひとみし}り: shyness around strangers — nervousness with unfamiliar people specifically
